title: Email: Fw: Great job in 2019/staff moves

content.text:
From: Thomas, Christopher <cdthomas@freepress.com>
Sent: Friday, January 3, 2020 12:26 PM
To: Albom, Mitch <malbom@freepress.com>; Alter, Marlowe <malter@freepress.com>; Birkett, David <dbirkett@freepress.com>; Crawford, Kirkland <kcrawford@freepress.com>; Ellis, Vince <vellis@freepress.com>; Fenech, Anthony <afenech@freepress.com>; Ford, Ryan <rford@freepress.com>; Monarrez, Carlos <cmonarrez@freepress.com>; Sabin, Rainer <RSabin@freepress.com>; Sang, Orion <OSang@freepress.com>; Seidel, Jeff <jseidel@freepress.com>; Solari, Chris <CSOLARI@lsj.com>; St. James, Helene <hstjames@freepress.com>; Sung, Elaine <ESung@freepress.com>; Windsor, Shawn <swindsor@freepress.com>
Subject: Great job in 2019/staff moves 
 
All: As I sift through the data from 2019, I want to say thanks to everyone for an impressive year.
We managed moderate gains YOY, despite having to make up nearly 13M from former staffers, and almost every staff writer generated more story views  than in 2018.

I hope to have a full report in the coming weeks, with some suggestions on how we can increase audience in 2019. We must continue to aggressively seek unique angles, analysis and enterprise and lead the charge creating conversations in our market. You guys are the best at doing this, and I can’t thank you enough.
In addition, we’re making a few tweaks on staff.

First: By now you’ve heard Vince Ellis has accepted a voluntary buyout and will leave the Free Press in February. This was a decision Vince had been thinking about for a while, and if you read the report in Crains about Freep staff changes last month, you know it’s a decision he’s at peace with. Vince owned the Pistons beat for us for a decade, and I’ll miss watching him crush the folks upstairs literally every single day. Please wish Vince well. He was gracious enough to stay through the NBA trade deadline. His last day is Feb. 17 (I believe).

Second: Vince’s departure allows us to think outside the box with how we fill the position. And so we’re sliding Anthony Fenech over to Pistons from the Tigers beat. He will step in and begin turning the screws on the Pistons after Vince’s last day, and he’ll also begin pursuing the type of heavy-hitting enterprise that satisfies his journalistic soul. Anthony has long said he wanted to broaden his reporting scope at the Free Press, and we agreed this move could put him on the path to doing that. Which means you’ll see Anthony still pursuing untold stories on the Tigers, Pistons, or other beats if there’s a good enough story. Anthony and I already are brainstorming names for a Tigers beat writer. If anyone comes to mind, please let one of us know.
Thanks again for your hard work.
You guys are going to crush 2020.
Great Lakes regional sports director, USA TODAY Network
